#!/bin/sh
# Flux batch script converted from LSF

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# LSF resources:
#   -J PCC_optimzer
#   -q elektro
#   -n 1
#   -R "rusage[mem=2GB]"
#   -M 10GB
#   -W 20:00
#   -u alherm@dtu.dk
#   -B / -N (mail at begin/end)
#   -o output_alex_run1.out
#   -e error_alex_run1.err
#   -R "span[hosts=1]"

#flux: --job-name=PCC_optimzer
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: --time-limit=20h
#flux: --output=output_alex_run1.out
#flux: --error=error_alex_run1.err

# Omitted LSF options: -R "rusage[mem=2GB]" and -M 10GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted LSF option: -q elektro (queue)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different priority/limits or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted LSF options: -u / -B / -N (email notifications)
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

module load cvx
module load mosek/9.2
##module load gurobi/8.1.1

matlab -nodisplay -r RUN_PCC_optim -logfile PCC_optim_logfile_output

reasons: LSF specified memory requirements (`-R "rusage[mem=2GB]"` and `-M 10GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.

LSF specified a queue (`-q elektro`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
